c.tagline: Southern Thailand's mainland gateway to Samui, Pha Ngan and Tao.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis are rare here; songthaews (shared pickup trucks) run fixed routes for a set fare, and tuk-tuks and motorbike taxis are negotiated. Grab is the easiest option for a fixed up-front price.

emergency.note: 191 for police, 1669 for medical/ambulance; Tourist Police 1155 (English-speaking).

hood_landmark.City Centre (Talat): Surat Thani night market Ta Pi river

avoid.reason: Beware overpriced or misleading combo bus-ferry ticket touts around the train station and piers, and keep valuables on you during overnight buses.

hood_desc: The compact downtown around the Talat (central market) and Ta Pi riverfront, home to the buzzing night markets, banks and travel agents; the walkable base for anyone overnighting before a ferry.

The old waterfront quarter along the Ta Pi River where Tapi and Ban Don piers send high-speed catamarans and overnight boats to the islands; workaday and local, handy if you have an early or late boat.

The transport hub around the Talat Kaset 1 and 2 bus terminals and the Central Plaza mall, where buses and minivans leave for Bangkok, Phuket and Krabi; functional but convenient for onward connections and shopping.
The railway town about 13 km west, built around Surat Thani Railway Station on the Southern Line to Bangkok; a quiet, practical base for train travelers rather than a destination in itself.
A calm riverside residential subdistrict near the Ta Pi River and the City Pillar Shrine, with local temples and a slower pace; suits travelers wanting a quieter, more authentic stay near town.

water.note: Drink bottled water; tap water is not potable.

transit.pay: Songthaews and local buses are cash-only, paid to the driver - a flat few-baht fare per ride. Island ferry and bus-boat combo tickets (Lomprayah, Seatran, Raja) are bought at pier offices, travel agents or online. Grab covers the town for app-based rides.
transit.hours: Songthaews and buses run roughly dawn to evening; island ferries run mostly in daylight, with a few overnight boats from Ban Don Pier. Taxis and Grab fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Surat Thani has no metro, and the main railway station is 13 km west at Phunphin. Getting around town is by songthaew, local bus, tuk-tuk and motorbike taxi, plus Grab. The town's real role is as the mainland ferry gateway to Ko Samui, Ko Pha Ngan and Ko Tao - high-speed catamarans leave Tapi Pier while Seatran and Raja run from the Don Sak piers east of the city.

train: Surat Thani Railway Station (Phunphin, 13 km west; Southern Line to/from Bangkok)
bus: Talat Kaset 1 & 2 terminals (buses & minivans to Bangkok, Phuket, Krabi and Nakhon Si Thammarat)
ferry: Tapi Pier & Ban Don Pier (city); Don Sak piers 65 km east - ferries to Ko Samui, Ko Pha Ngan and Ko Tao

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus/van to the city center (35-45 min)
Combined airport-to-pier van & ferry ticket to Ko Samui

tip.r: ~5-10% at sit-down restaurants; not expected at markets or for street food.

food.name: Khai Khem Chaiya (Chaiya salted eggs)
food.desc: Duck eggs cured in salted red clay in nearby Chaiya district, giving a jewel-orange, oily yolk. Eaten with rice congee or stirred through stir-fries.

places.name: Lam Phu 2
places.note: Michelin-listed riverside kitchen whose stir-fried squid with salted egg is the signature.

places.name: Lucky Restaurant
places.note: Family-run Thai-Chinese place; chef shops the market daily for salted duck egg dishes.

places.name: Talat Kaset municipal market
places.area: Ban Don, near the bus terminals
places.note: Stalls sell Chaiya salted eggs loose and cooked into rice plates; best place to buy some to take.

food.name: Hoi Nang Rom and Hoi Tod (oysters)
food.desc: Kanchanadit oysters are among Thailand's best. Eaten raw with lime, chilli and fried shallots, or fried into a crisp-edged oyster omelette.

places.name: Lam Phu 2
places.note: Oyster omelette with a crackly egg base and very fresh local oysters; river view tables.

places.name: San Chao night market
places.note: Evening riverfront market with seafood grills doing oysters by the plate at low prices.

places.name: Kanchanadit oyster shacks
places.note: Roadside shacks beside the oyster beds themselves; as fresh as it gets, cash only.

food.name: Kaeng Tai Pla
food.desc: The fiercest southern curry: fermented fish innards, turmeric, chilli and bamboo shoots. Pungent, salty and seriously hot; order rice alongside.

places.name: Municipal fresh market curry stalls
places.note: Rows of khao kaeng trays where you point at southern curries by the ladle.

places.name: Lucky Restaurant
places.note: Cooks proper southern curries to order, including milder versions for visitors.

places.name: Talat Kaset 2 food row
places.note: Late-running local stalls with tai pla and other southern curries over rice.

food.name: Sakuu Sai Muu
food.desc: Translucent sago dumplings stuffed with sweet-savoury minced pork, peanut and palm sugar, served with lettuce, coriander and raw chilli.

places.name: Municipal fresh market
places.note: Morning stalls sell them by the bag; a classic Surat Thani snack to eat while walking.

places.name: Soi Tonpo street food market
places.area: Soi Tonpo, near the Tapi River
places.note: Evening market row with sago dumplings alongside satay, papaya salad and grilled fish.

places.name: San Chao night market
places.note: Snack vendors here keep them fresh-steamed through the evening.

food.name: Khao Yam Pak Tai
food.desc: Southern rice salad: herb-tinted rice tossed at the table with shredded coconut, lemongrass, kaffir lime, pomelo, dried shrimp and budu dressing.

places.name: Municipal fresh market breakfast stalls
places.note: Sold in the early morning only; ask for the budu sauce on the side if you are unsure.

places.name: Lucky Restaurant
places.note: One of the few sit-down places in town that plates khao yam properly with all the garnishes.

places.name: Talat Kaset 1 market
places.note: Cheap, generous plates from vendors serving the morning bus-station crowd.

food.name: Roti and Kaeng for Breakfast
food.desc: Muslim-southern morning ritual: flaky griddled roti torn into a bowl of mild chicken or goat curry, or served plain with sugar and condensed milk.

places.name: Roti stalls, Talat Kaset area
places.area: Ban Don, near the bus stations
places.note: Early-morning griddles beside the market; roti kaeng from around 6am until sold out.

places.name: Ban Don riverfront kopitiam shops
places.note: Old shophouse coffee shops pairing roti with southern-style hot tea and coffee.

places.name: Soi Tonpo street food market
places.note: Evening roti carts do the sweet banana-and-condensed-milk version for dessert.

food.name: Cha Chak (southern pulled milk tea)
food.desc: Strong black tea pulled between two vessels with condensed and evaporated milk until foamy. Order it hot, or yen over ice.

places.name: Ban Don kopitiam shops
places.note: Old-school coffee shops where the tea is still pulled by hand at the counter.

places.name: Talat Kaset market drink stalls
places.area: Ban Don, near the bus terminals
places.note: Bag-and-straw takeaway cha chak for a few baht before a ferry or bus.

places.name: San Chao night market
places.note: Evening stalls do both cha chak and the coffee version, oliang, over crushed ice.

food.name: Nam Maphrao (young coconut water)
food.desc: Surat Thani province is Thailand's coconut heartland. Drink it straight from a chilled young nut, then scrape out the soft flesh.

places.name: Talat Kaset 1 market
places.note: Vendors hack open chilled nuts to order; cheaper than anywhere on the islands.

places.name: San Chao night market
places.note: Riverside stalls sell coconut water alongside grilled seafood in the evening.

places.name: Don Sak pier stalls
places.note: Handy last stop for a cold coconut before the boat to Samui or Pha Ngan.

landmarks: Surat Thani City Pillar Shrine (San Lak Mueang)
The city's ornate spiritual heart, a gleaming Srivijaya-style shrine of stacked golden spires that honours Surat Thani's ancient Buddhist heritage.
Wat Phra Borommathat Chaiya
A revered 1,200-year-old Srivijaya-era chedi in nearby Chaiya, among Thailand's oldest religious monuments and the south's most sacred pilgrimage site.
Suan Mokkh (Wat Suan Mokkhaphalaram)
The forest monastery founded by reformer Buddhadasa Bhikkhu, world-famous for meditation retreats amid tranquil coconut groves and spiritual sculpture gardens.
Cheow Lan Lake and Ratchaprapha Dam
An emerald reservoir studded with limestone karsts rising sheer from jade waters, Thailand's answer to Guilin, with floating raft-house bungalows.
Khao Sok National Park
One of the world's oldest rainforests, a day trip west of the city, sheltering wild elephants, gibbons and the giant Rafflesia flower.
Ko Lamphu Park
A leafy island park in the middle of the Tapi River, reached by footbridge, where locals jog and picnic with skyline views.
Bang Bai Mai Floating Community
A canal-side village of stilt houses and coconut orchards where longtail boats glide past traditional southern Thai life and weekend floating markets.
Khao Tha Phet Viewpoint
A forested hill south of town crowned by a Buddhist stupa, offering panoramic views over the Tapi River delta and Gulf coast.
Chaiya National Museum
A fine collection of Srivijaya bronzes and artefacts beside the great Chaiya chedi, illuminating the empire that once ruled these coasts.
Tapi Riverfront and San Chao Night Market
Surat Thani's liveliest evening scene, where riverside food stalls near the Chinese shrine dish up southern curries, seafood and roti.

intl.to: Butterworth / Penang (Malaysia) - change at Hat Yai and Padang Besar

train.note: Surat Thani is the southern gateway junction. Overnight sleepers from Bangkok take about 9-11 hours to Phun Phin station, 12 km west of the town, and southbound trains continue to Hat Yai for the Malaysian connection at Padang Besar - there is no through carriage, so you change. Book on the SRT D-Ticket site up to 90 days ahead; lower berths go first. Combined train-and-boat tickets to Ko Samui and Ko Pha Ngan are sold at the station.

intl.to: Penang & Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia) - via Hat Yai and the Sadao border
intl.op: Thai and Malaysian coach operators — booked through 12Go (https://12go.asia/)

bus.note: The Malaysia coaches usually mean a change in Hat Yai and a long border stop - budget a full day. Domestic services from the Surat Thani terminal reach Bangkok overnight in about 10 hours, Phuket in 5 and Krabi in 3, on Transport Co. (https://www.transport.co.th/) and private operators. Shuttle buses connect the train station, the airport and the Donsak ferry pier.

intl.to: Ko Samui, Ko Pha Ngan & Ko Tao (Thailand) - car ferry from Donsak, ~60 km east
Ko Samui & Ko Pha Ngan (Thailand) - from Donsak
Ko Tao & Ko Pha Ngan (Thailand) - night boat from Ban Don pier in town

ferry.note: There are no international sailings. The main island ferries leave from Donsak, about an hour east of town, with connecting buses timed to the sailings and sold as combined tickets. The old wooden night boat from Ban Don pier in Surat Thani itself is slower and basic but leaves late and saves a night's accommodation. Crossings are reduced or cancelled during the October-December monsoon.

half.name: Ko Samui
half.blurb: Island reached by ferry from the mainland pier, known for its beaches and coconut plantations.

half.name: Ko Pha Ngan
half.blurb: Island reached by ferry, known for its beaches and monthly Full Moon Party gathering.

full.name: Nakhon Si Thammarat
full.blurb: Old southern city with a revered Buddhist temple and a long tradition of shadow puppet theater.

full.name: Krabi
full.blurb: Coastal province known for limestone cliffs and longtail boat trips out to nearby islands.
